narrative:
The model predicts an 80% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This high probability means the system sees strong signs that you are likely to depart soon, based on patterns from many similar employees.

Three factors stood out most in driving this prediction. First, having received other job opportunities while at your current company was the strongest influence pushing toward leaving. Most employees predicted to stay had not received any outside offers, but you have, and this strongly signals higher risk of departure.

Second, your overall years of experience (6-10 years) also pushed the prediction toward leaving. While this is fairly common—about 35% of employees predicted to stay fall in the same range—it still contributed noticeably to the model's view that you may be ready for a change.

Third, working in the "other" sector rather than medical or education fields added further weight toward leaving. Only about 22% of employees the model expects to stay work in this broader category, making your sector a moderate contributor to the higher risk score.

Taken together, these elements created a clear picture for the system. The organization should discuss your external opportunities and long-term goals with you openly. You may want to reflect on whether your current role still aligns with your career plans, especially given the outside interest you have received. Addressing these points could either change the outlook or help you make a confident next step. (248 words)
